toegepas.voor: Dit het in die 15de en 16de eeu
toegepas.na: Die Renaissance het in die 15de en 16de eeu
toegepas.rede_vinder: 'Dit' grammatically points back to 'n woord', but a word did not happen in the 15th century; name the subject.
toegepas.fout: 'Dit' grammatically points back to 'n woord', so the sentence says a word happened in the 15th and 16th century.
toegepas.rede_keurder: Naming the Renaissance as subject fixes the reference without adding or moving anything.

toegepas.voor: geweet en gemaak en gebou het
toegepas.rede_vinder: A three-item list reads more smoothly with a comma and one 'en' than with 'en ... en'.
toegepas.fout: The 'en ... en' chain in a three-item list reads wooden in expository text.
toegepas.rede_keurder: Comma plus one 'en' is the normal Afrikaans list form and the meaning is unchanged.

toegepas.voor: hulle hele dag aan kuns en aan kennis gee
toegepas.na: hulle hele dag aan kuns en kennis wy
toegepas.rede_vinder: 'Jou dag aan iets gee' mirrors English 'give one's day to'; Afrikaans says 'aan iets wy'.
toegepas.fout: 'Jou dag aan iets gee' copies English 'give one's day to'; Afrikaans says 'aan iets wy'.
toegepas.rede_keurder: 'Wy' is the natural fixed expression and keeps the meaning exactly.

toegepas.blok: 'n Nuwe manier om 'n vraag te antwoord
toegepas.voor: Party kere het hulle eie oë iets anders as die ou boek gewys.
toegepas.na: Party kere het hulle met hulle eie oë iets anders gesien as wat in die ou boek gestaan het.
toegepas.rede_vinder: Eyes 'showing something other than the book' is a wooden construction; seeing with one's own eyes is the natural idiom and keeps the meaning.
toegepas.fout: 'Hulle eie oë het iets anders as die ou boek gewys' is a stiff construction that compares eyes to a book.
toegepas.rede_keurder: Seeing with one's own eyes something other than what stood in the book is the natural idiom, same meaning, and the next sentence still follows.

toegepas.rede_vinder: People who design buildings are 'boumeesters'; 'bouers' are those who build them.
toegepas.fout: 'Bouers' are the people who build; the sentence is about designing.
toegepas.rede_keurder: 'Boumeesters' is the exact word for those who designed buildings and adds no fact.

toegepas.voor: In hierdie tyd het party hulle op nuwe maniere bestudeer.
toegepas.na: In hierdie tyd het party mense dit op nuwe maniere bestudeer.
toegepas.rede_vinder: 'party hulle' reads as 'some of them' and leaves unclear who studied what; 'party mense dit' makes subject and object clear.
toegepas.fout: 'party hulle' first reads as 'some of them', so subject and object are unclear.
toegepas.rede_keurder: 'party mense dit' makes clear who studied and what, with 'dit' summing up the listed things; meaning unchanged.

laat_vaar.voor: 'n Kunstenaar of 'n geleerde moet ook elke dag eet en slaap.
laat_vaar.na: 'n Kunstenaar of 'n geleerde moes ook elke dag eet en slaap.
laat_vaar.rede_vinder: The surrounding sentences narrate the past, so the present 'moet' jars; 'moes' keeps the tense consistent.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: The present 'moet' states a general truth about any artist or scholar, which is natural Afrikaans; the change is lateral.

na_skrywer.voor: waarin dinge ver weg kleiner lyk
na_skrywer.na: waarin dinge wat ver weg is, kleiner lyk
na_skrywer.rede_vinder: 'dinge ver weg' is clipped; a relative clause reads naturally and the comma closes the embedded clause.
na_skrywer.fout: 'dinge ver weg' in the definition is clipped.
na_skrywer.rede_keurder: It is a glossary definition, so any rewording beyond a plain error goes through the writer.
na_skrywer.waarom: the reviewer sent it to the writer

vlae.teks: Ryk handelaars en die leiers van die stad het hulle daarvoor betaal.
vlae.rede: 'daarvoor' grammatically points to eating and sleeping in the previous sentence, so it reads as if they were paid to eat and sleep; the intended object (paying them so they could work at art and learning) cannot be named without guessing the writer's wording.
